text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging SRE oncall — elevated 5xx rate for /v1/generate in us-west-2 (5xx% ~ 11% over last 5m). Alert id: alert-22345.
maya: ack, on it. pulling up dashboards.
Liam: I see a sharp bump starting ~2234506500. Latency p95 also up, lots of upstream 502s from gateway.
Amal: checking kv/prefix metrics — prefix_cache.miss_rate spiked to 42% on shard-7, eviction_rate extremely high. slab_alloc_fail counter incrementing.
Jun: logs from kv-daemon on shard-7 show repeated: `ERR slab_alloc_fail: requested 1048576, free 0` and `LRU churning: evicted 128k entries/sec`
maya: hmm. sounds like a hot shard causing churn and cache thrashing -> backend timeouts -> gateway 502s. any recent deploys?
Liam: no deploys in the window. config changes? not that I can see.
Amal: possible hot key pattern, maybe some client started scanning prefixes. I can run `kvctl prefix-stats shard-7` for top prefixes.
maya: do it. also let’s notify support that customers may see 5xx/timeouts.
Amal: running:```bash
kvctl prefix-stats --shard=7 --top=20
# returning heavy counts for prefix: user:/uploads/large-batch/*
```
Jun: yep, one prefix is responsible for ~60% of cache lookups. likely a batch job hammering that range.
maya: mitigation plan: 1) throttle requests to that prefix at the edge; 2) temporarily bypass prefix cache for shard-7 or reduce slab size; 3) roll traffic to other shards if possible. opinions?
Liam: edge throttle first — less blast radius. ops-bot can we apply rate-limit rule for path matching the prefix?
ops-bot: ran `edgectl add-rule --match "path_regex:(/v1/generate.*user:/uploads/large-batch)" --rate 10r/s --duration 600s` — rule pushed to us-west-2.
maya: good. Amal, how risky is toggling prefix cache off for shard-7?
Amal: toggling prefix cache off will increase direct kv reads but should stop eviction storm. risk: higher backend IO, possible latency increase for other clients, but preferable to 502s. we can do it on one shard.
Jun: recommend do toggle + spike protection: set `prefix_cache.enabled=false` for shard-7 and enable `direct_kv_burst_limit` on frontends.
Liam: ok. oncall-manager — do we have approval to change cache config in prod for a single shard?
oncall-manager: emergency mitigation ok, document in incident ticket and notify infra. keep change scoped and revert after stabilization.
maya: applying change now. command:```bash
infractl update-config --path "/clusters/us-west-2/shards/7/prefix_cache/enabled" --value false --reason "eviction-thrash emergency"
```
ops-bot: config update accepted, rolling to shard-7 prefix cache workers (rolling restart).
Amal: I'm tailing kv-daemon logs. slab_alloc_fail counters dropping already. eviction_rate decreasing. miss_rate still elevated but trending down.
Jun: gateway 5xx% dropping: 11% -> 6% after throttle -> 2.2% after cache toggle. p95 latency improving.
Liam: pushing a traffic-routing policy to shift ~20% of new sessions away from shard-7 for safety. command: `routectl set-weight --shard=7 --weight=0.8`.
maya: support, message for customers?
ops-bot: drafted status blurb: "We experienced elevated 5xx errors in us-west-2 due to a hot key workload affecting internal cache. Mitigation in progress; some requests may be slower. Engineers are monitoring." want me to post?
maya: yes, post to status.redwood and ping CS for top accounts. add note to incident ticket.
Amal: running live debug: `kvctl dump-lru --shard=7 --limit=50` shows top items are indeed the same prefix. there are some unusually large entries — looks like clients are storing big blobs under prefix keys. possible regression in a client.
Jun: can we add a short-term size cap filter at the gateway to avoid caching huge blobs?
Liam: we can. `gatewayctl add-filter --max-cache-item-size=256KB --match-prefix user:/uploads/large-batch` — pushing now.
ops-bot: filter pushed, cache size-limited for that prefix.
maya: monitoring heatmap — backend ops IO increased but error curve holding down. any customer impact numbers?
Amal: support metrics: ~1200 failed requests total in 5m window across us-west-2, affecting ~4 customers (by volume). top affected: partner-acct-23 and internal-e2e-tests.
maya: good catch. CS notified. we should capture root cause after stabilization: suspect a noisy client/bug.
Jun: agree — capturing a sample of offending requests and contacting the client owner. I'll create a short alert to flag prefix scan patterns.
Liam: once stable, we should revert prefix_cache.enabled back to true for shard-7 but with increased slab quota and add preemptive rate limiting for that prefix.
ops-bot: observed overall 5xx back to baseline <1% for region.
maya: ok, moving to recovery -> monitor phase. please add timeline & action items to incident ticket 22345.
Amal: logged mitigation steps, commands executed, and top traces. I'll keep watching for 30m then start rollback plan.
Jun: follow-up actions for follow-up doc: contact client owning large-batch prefix, add automated detection for hot-prefix, implement per-prefix size caps and slab growth policy.
Liam: thumbs up. post-mortem owner? maya?
maya: happy to own. assigning to myself and Amal. will schedule postmortem meeting tomorrow.
oncall-manager: thanks team. great quick coordination. close on-call handoff in 10m if stable. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: incident 22345 status -> mitigated (5xx% returned to baseline).
maya: thread for timeline + artifacts in incident ticket. closing thread here, will update once postmortem is scheduled. :white_check_mark:
